reference_diagnosis.name: Functional movement disorder (functional tremor with functional dystonia)
reference_diagnosis.basis: Positive clinical signs: abrupt onset after minor injury, entrainment, distractibility, variability, co-activation, give-way weakness, spontaneous remissions; normal DaT-SPECT.

competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: Evening worsening here is fatigue-linked and inconsistent; abrupt onset; positive functional signs; spontaneous remission

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Onset after wrist injury with fist posture
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: No pain, swelling, colour or temperature change; posture resolves with distraction

key_evidence_gaps.question: Tremor analysis/accelerometry
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Objective support for entrainment and frequency variability

key_evidence_gaps.question: DaT-SPECT if parkinsonism remains a concern

held_out_evidence.result: Frequency entrainment and pause during ballistic movements of the other hand.

discriminating_investigations.investigation: Structured examination for positive functional signs
Levodopa trial only if diurnal pattern is consistent and functional signs absent

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Anchoring on DRD because of evening worsening and the patient's request
Diagnosing FMD as exclusion, or because of stress/depression, instead of from positive signs
Dismissing symptoms as not real; language must remain respectful
Ordering extensive genetic testing without clinical justification
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
clinician_review_notes: DRAFT. Wiki to check clinical plausibility, findings, held-out results, and red flags.
